subject: english
stem: An engineer tried to ___ the noise from a ventilation fan by fitting its housing with acoustic panels.
explanation: Reduce means make less, consistent with the purpose of the panels.

subject: english
stem: The tree-ring patterns ___ periods of drought: narrow rings generally formed in years with little rainfall.
explanation: Mirror means reflect or correspond to a pattern; the rings track environmental conditions.

subject: english
stem: Although the trail looked ___ from the entrance, several steep slopes emerged farther along.
explanation: The contrast with steep slopes indicates a seemingly flat trail.

subject: english
stem: The proposal was not entirely ___; despite disagreements about cost, every committee member supported its safety goals.
explanation: The concession that members supported part of the proposal rules out complete rejection.

subject: english
stem: Nadia had wanted to leave the family bakery, yet she paused outside its door, smiling at the warm light while checking the train schedule again. The passage mainly conveys Nadia's

options.label: A
options.text: conflicting attachment and desire for change

options.label: B
options.text: certainty that the bakery will close

explanation: Her smile signals attachment while the schedule signals anticipation of leaving.

subject: english
stem: The poem opens by comparing a lake to polished glass, then asks why its surface conceals so much life. The shift chiefly moves from

options.label: B
options.text: a personal memory to historical evidence

options.label: D
options.text: a conflict to an explicit resolution

explanation: The shift changes from describing a surface to questioning what it hides.

subject: english
stem: A speaker calls the city's library a 'locked gate' but then lists its free workshops and open doors, arguing that the metaphor misleads. Why invoke the gate?

options.label: A
options.text: To challenge the idea that the library excludes residents

options.label: B
options.text: To claim all buildings need stronger locks

explanation: The speaker introduces a metaphor of exclusion to rebut it with counterexamples.

subject: english
stem: Some birds relocate seasonally. For example, swallows travel hundreds of miles when insects become scarce. What is the function of the second sentence?

options.label: D
options.text: It explains why all birds remain stationary.

explanation: The swallow is a specific instance of seasonal relocation.

subject: english
stem: Text 1 argues that early villages formed only after farming became widespread. Text 2 cites evidence of permanent settlements supported mainly by fishing before intensive farming. Text 2 primarily

options.label: A
options.text: challenges the sequence asserted in Text 1

explanation: The second account offers a potentially earlier route to settlement.

subject: english
stem: Elena returned every lost item she found and stayed late to help neighbors repair bicycles. These details characterize her as
explanation: Her repeated considerate actions support helpfulness.

subject: english
stem: A writer says memories are 'seeds stored beneath winter soil.' The comparison suggests memories

options.label: A
options.text: can persist quietly and later grow vivid

explanation: Dormant seeds evoke memories that remain latent but may reemerge.

subject: english
stem: When Tom's younger cousin struggled with a puzzle, Tom offered a hint but allowed the cousin to finish it independently. The central idea is that Tom
explanation: His limited hint encourages the cousin's independence.

subject: english
stem: A survey records bicycles on three paths: North 46, Creek 31, Hill 58. Which statement is supported?

options.label: A
options.text: Hill had the most recorded bicycles.

options.label: D
options.text: All three paths had equal totals.

explanation: 58 is greater than 46 and 31.

subject: english
stem: For four years, two populations of insects were observed. Population A rose from 80 to 160; B declined from 150 to 90. Which result supports a claim that their trends diverged?

options.label: B
options.text: Both increased by the same amount.

options.label: D
options.text: B increased more rapidly than A.

explanation: The populations changed in opposite directions.

subject: english
stem: A materials study compared panels of equal area. At 10°C, panel X lost 12 units of heat and Y lost 21; at 20°C, X lost 18 and Y lost 25. Which conclusion is supported?

options.label: A
options.text: X lost less heat than Y at both temperatures.

options.label: B
options.text: X lost more heat at 20°C than Y did.

options.label: C
options.text: Temperature did not affect either panel.

options.label: D
options.text: Y lost exactly twice as much as X at both temperatures.

explanation: Each matched-temperature comparison shows a smaller loss for X.

subject: english
stem: A historian argues that a mural was designed collectively. Which account best supports the claim?

options.label: A
options.text: Several artists planned the layout together and signed the completed work.

options.label: B
options.text: One artist barred others from the studio.

options.label: C
options.text: The mural remained unfinished for decades.

options.label: D
options.text: No records identify where the mural was installed.

explanation: Joint planning is direct evidence for shared creation.

subject: english
stem: A researcher predicts a mineral additive benefits all seedlings equally. In an experiment, seedlings from species A grew 20% more with the additive, but species B grew no more than untreated B seedlings. The result

options.label: A
options.text: challenges the claim of equal benefit

options.label: D
options.text: rules out any benefit to A

explanation: The two species respond differently under the treatment.

subject: english
stem: Excavators found matching decorative marks on objects from distant sites, but none at settlements between them. What is the most cautious inference?

options.label: A
options.text: The sites may have exchanged ideas through a network not yet fully documented.

options.label: B
options.text: The two settlements certainly had identical governments.

options.label: C
options.text: Every society used these same marks.

options.label: D
options.text: The marks prove the objects were made in one workshop.

explanation: Shared symbolism is consistent with cultural contact but does not establish a precise mechanism.

subject: english
stem: At the science fair, the two ___ presentations explained different approaches to water filtration.
explanation: The presentations belong to two teams, requiring the plural possessive teams'.

subject: english
stem: Each Monday, a technician ___ the weather sensors for damage.
explanation: Each Monday describes a habitual action, so the present-tense singular verb checks fits.

subject: english
stem: The bridge was closed overnight ___ workers inspected its supporting cables the next morning.
explanation: A period correctly separates two complete sentences; the alternatives lack appropriate joining punctuation in this construction.

subject: english
stem: The sequence of color-coded labels ___ the technicians locate every storage bin.
explanation: The singular head noun sequence takes helps.

subject: english
stem: The sketches were submitted on Friday ___ the judges announced the finalists on Monday.
explanation: A semicolon joins the two independent clauses.

subject: english
stem: Walking across the courtyard, ___ spotted a loose stone near the fountain.
explanation: The introductory modifier must describe the person walking.

subject: english
stem: The workshop included designers from Quito, Ecuador; Dakar, Senegal; and ___ .
explanation: Semicolons separate complex list items that contain internal commas.

subject: english
stem: The device was inexpensive ___ however, it required frequent maintenance.
explanation: A semicolon before however separates independent clauses; a comma after however is also needed in the completed sentence.

subject: english
stem: The instruments were calibrated; ___, the team started collecting measurements.
explanation: Finally fits the last step of a sequence.

subject: english
stem: The map originally suggested a single entrance. ___, a later inspection revealed three entrances.
explanation: However signals that new evidence contradicts an earlier belief.

subject: english
stem: The park includes a rain garden. ___, its paths use permeable paving to absorb runoff.
explanation: Additionally introduces a second related feature.

subject: english
stem: The soil dried during the heat wave. ___, the seedlings required more frequent watering.
explanation: Consequently expresses a result of the drying.

subject: english
stem: Notes: Paper maps require printed updates; digital maps can display new closures immediately. Which sentence highlights a difference?

options.label: A
options.text: Unlike printed maps, digital maps can reflect newly reported closures without reprinting.

options.label: B
options.text: Both kinds of maps help visitors find routes.

explanation: The sentence explicitly contrasts update methods.

subject: english
stem: Notes: Sculptor Lina Chen assembles discarded glass into hanging forms; her work Lantern Current casts moving shadows. Which introduction is best for an unfamiliar audience?

options.label: A
options.text: In Lantern Current, sculptor Lina Chen uses recycled glass to create hanging forms and shifting shadows.

options.label: B
options.text: The artist's newest work is impressive.

options.label: C
options.text: Chen's piece differs from her earlier ones.

options.label: D
options.text: It was displayed at a recent event.

explanation: The sentence identifies the artist and work and explains the artwork to newcomers.

subject: english
stem: Notes: Eighty volunteers planted native shrubs; 75% survived a dry summer; watered plots had higher survival than unwatered plots. Which sentence best introduces the results?

options.label: A
options.text: A volunteer planting project found 75% shrub survival, with higher survival in watered plots.

options.label: B
options.text: The volunteers worked on a summer project.

options.label: C
options.text: Some shrubs require more water than others.

options.label: D
options.text: Native shrubs can be planted in many places.

explanation: The sentence summarizes the documented outcome and key comparison.

subject: english
stem: Demand for reusable containers has increased as cafes offer deposit returns. Analysts expect the market to ___ as more locations adopt the program.
explanation: Expand is consistent with more locations and growing demand.

subject: english
stem: When the prototype failed, Priya took a ___ approach, testing one component at a time instead of replacing the entire device.
explanation: Testing sequentially is a methodical troubleshooting strategy.

subject: english
stem: Using high-resolution microscopes, scientists can ___ tiny cracks that ordinary cameras cannot reveal.
explanation: Detect means observe or discover a feature.

subject: english
stem: Compared with the ancestral bone, the newer fossil has a more ___ joint that allows rotation through a wider angle.
explanation: Greater allowable rotation indicates greater flexibility.

subject: english
stem: References to the sea are not ___ in these poems; they appear in nearly every stanza.
explanation: Not rare is consistent with near-constant appearance.

subject: english
stem: A ceramic artist mixes pigments with clay before firing; heat then ___ the mixture into a durable finish.
explanation: Transforms indicates a change into a new material state.

subject: english
stem: The researchers ___ installing additional sensors because the existing network left large gaps in coverage.
explanation: Advocating means supporting a proposed measure.

subject: english
stem: The report did not ___ the disputed claim; instead, it noted that key archival records were missing.
explanation: Substantiate means provide evidence establishing a claim.

subject: english
stem: After discussing how urban animals adapt, the author describes foxes using railway embankments as nighttime paths. This detail serves to
explanation: The foxes give a concrete example of the preceding general point.

subject: english
stem: Observers recorded how often bees landed on blue and yellow paper flowers. What did researchers directly measure?
explanation: The recorded behavior is landings by color.

subject: english
stem: A researcher claims quieter classrooms always improve recall. Two equal groups studied the same material; the group with moderate background noise recalled more. This finding

options.label: C
options.text: establishes that all noise helps everyone

explanation: Better recall with moderate noise is counterevidence to an always-claim.

subject: english
stem: A character is described as 'quick to laugh at mistakes' but also 'the first to apologize for her own.' Which quotation best supports a claim of playful yet responsible behavior?

options.label: A
options.text: She joked about the spilled paint and then stayed to clean it.

options.label: B
options.text: She stayed silent throughout the meeting.

options.label: C
options.text: She refused to revisit the incident.

options.label: D
options.text: She left before anyone noticed the spill.

explanation: Humor paired with cleaning up demonstrates both traits.

subject: english
stem: Two regions tracked energy prices: in North, prices rose 3%, 6%, and 9% over three years; in South, 8%, 4%, and 1%. Which comparison is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: North's increases accelerated while South's slowed.

options.label: B
options.text: Both showed steady increases in the rate.

explanation: North's sequence rises and South's falls.

subject: english
stem: A debate asked whether street trees lower summer temperatures. One researcher cited shaded sidewalk measurements; another noted that tree type and spacing varied. What does the second researcher emphasize?

options.label: A
options.text: A possible confounding factor in the evidence

options.label: C
options.text: That all trees have identical effects

explanation: Different planting patterns complicate a simple inference.

subject: english
stem: A character says, 'I could have taken the road that opened before me, but fear held the map.' This image most directly expresses
explanation: The road represents an opportunity and fear prevented taking it.

subject: english
stem: An essay compares folktales and science fiction, noting that both examine choices but only one commonly invents future technologies. Which conclusion follows?

options.label: A
options.text: Genres can share themes while differing in typical settings.

options.label: D
options.text: Science fiction cannot depict ethical decisions.

explanation: The given comparison allows overlap in concerns alongside a difference in conventions.

subject: english
stem: Genetic similarities among populations on two islands, paired with dated settlement remains, suggest contact occurred before a later documented trade route. The evidence most reasonably indicates

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: all island inhabitants arrived in one voyage

options.label: D
options.text: genetic evidence provides an exact sailing date

explanation: Genetics and chronology support early contact without specifying exact journeys.

subject: english
stem: To estimate a tutoring program's effect, researchers randomly assigned eligible students to either tutoring or existing study hall. Why was this design useful?

options.label: A
options.text: Random assignment helps make the groups comparable before the program.

options.label: C
options.text: It removes the need to measure outcomes.

options.label: D
options.text: It proves tutoring cannot affect results.

explanation: Random assignment reduces systematic preexisting group differences.

subject: english
stem: The two ___ decisions were presented to the school board separately.
explanation: Two committees jointly require the plural possessive committees'.

subject: english
stem: The team attributed the discrepancy ___ a sensor that had not been recalibrated.
explanation: Attribute a result to a cause is the correct prepositional construction.

subject: english
stem: The volunteers who arrived early ___ assigned to prepare the tables.
explanation: The restrictive who-clause is not set off with punctuation.

subject: english
stem: The element carbon has a stable isotope, carbon-13, ___ scientists use in certain tracing studies.
explanation: Which introduces an additional clause here without corrupting the sentence structure.

subject: english
stem: The first system had a single backup battery ___ the revised system used two independent batteries.
explanation: Two independent clauses can be joined by a semicolon.

subject: english
stem: The group added soil sensors ___ identify which planters needed water.
explanation: The infinitive to identify expresses purpose.

subject: english
stem: After inspecting the cracked beam, ___ recommended reinforcing the support.
explanation: The inspecting subject must be the engineer.

subject: english
stem: One issue remained unresolved: ___ .

options.label: A
options.text: how to transport the equipment safely

explanation: The colon introduces an explanation of the one issue.

subject: english
stem: The manuscript was reviewed in March. ___, the publisher prepared it for printing in April.
explanation: Afterward conveys the next chronological step.

subject: english
stem: The town could widen the road. ___, it could reduce speeds through better intersections.
explanation: Alternatively offers a different solution.

subject: english
stem: Notes: A steel truss can span long distances with less material than a solid steel beam of similar capacity. Which sentence emphasizes its comparative advantage?

options.label: A
options.text: A truss can achieve a long span while using less steel than a comparable solid beam.

options.label: B
options.text: Steel is widely used in construction.

options.label: C
options.text: A bridge must carry its own weight.

explanation: The claim directly compares material efficiency.

subject: english
stem: Notes: Researchers define network effects as a service becoming more valuable when more people use it. The audience already knows social media apps. Which sentence introduces the concept best?

options.label: A
options.text: Just as a social platform becomes more useful when friends join, some services gain value as their user base grows.

options.label: B
options.text: A service is something users access.

options.label: D
options.text: Some people do not use social networks.

explanation: The familiar analogy illuminates the abstract effect.

subject: english
stem: Notes: Star K has a surface temperature of 5,000 K; star M has 8,000 K. Which sentence emphasizes the comparison?

options.label: A
options.text: Star M's surface temperature is 3,000 K higher than star K's.

options.label: D
options.text: Scientists classify stars using several properties.

explanation: The sentence explicitly quantifies the temperature difference.

subject: english
stem: Notes: The book Night Path is a mystery for middle-school readers; it follows a young cartographer decoding old trail markers. Which introduction is best?

options.label: A
options.text: Night Path is a middle-grade mystery about a young cartographer solving clues hidden in trail markers.

options.label: D
options.text: Readers may have different opinions about books.

explanation: The sentence provides audience, genre and premise.

subject: english
stem: Notes: Butterflies draw liquid nectar through a tube-like proboscis; hummingbirds use elongated tongues to collect nectar. Which sentence highlights a similarity?

options.text: Butterflies and hummingbirds are the same kind of animal.

explanation: Both descriptions involve adapted structures used to consume nectar.
